_readme: Canonical cross-platform contract for the sponsor-type pattern lists (issue #147).
This file is the single source of truth. Python and Swift (BioMedLit) each carry
their own transcription of these strings, and each platform's test suite asserts
its constants equal this file exactly. Editing one platform's list without editing
this file fails that platform's parity test; editing this file without updating the
other fails theirs. That is the point: silent divergence becomes impossible.
Android carries no funder or sponsor classifier, so it is not a party to this
contract — unlike data_availability_patterns.json, which binds all three.
The split into two halves is significant and is NOT merely presentational:
- determine_sponsor_type() / FundingAnalyzer.determineSponsorType tests the
government half first, so one public agency outranks any number of
universities alongside it.
- Their concatenation, in this order, is what classify_funder_name() /
FundingAnalyzer.classifyFunder matches to mean 'not industry'. Moving a
pattern between halves changes the sponsor tier; adding or removing one
changes the industry boundary, which is measured against funder_names.json.
Two entries are deliberate judgement calls rather than plain readings:
'wellcome' is a charitable foundation and 'medical research council' is a UK
research council, and both sit in the government half. Revisit on both platforms
or not at all.
Do not regenerate this file mechanically from any one platform. Change it by hand,
deliberately, as part of a change that touches both.
See doc/cross_platform/transparency_parity/README.md.
